headline: 1999 order sets health protection rules for service members taking part in certain military operations.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this executive order sets rules meant to better protect the health of military personnel who take part in particular military operations. It appears to deal with medical protections given to troops during those operations, such as drugs or vaccines meant to guard against threats like chemical or biological weapons. No official summary was provided, so the exact rules, including any consent requirements, cannot be confirmed here.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the US armed forces deployed in certain military operations
who_it_affects.how: The order sets health protection rules that apply to them during those operations.
The department is likely responsible for carrying out the health protection rules the order sets.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed September 30, 1999; exact effective date not stated in the provided material.
